rows.claim: Marx's full sentence frames religion as both symptom and solace, not merely a con: 'Religion is the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world, and the soul of soulless conditions. It is the opium of the people.'
rows.sourceTitle: Opium of the people - Wikipedia
rows.note: German original: 'Die Religion ... ist das Opium des Volkes.' Passage occurs in the introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right.

rows.claim: Publication of the essay containing the line, in Marx's journal co-edited with Arnold Ruge
rows.sourceTitle: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right - Wikipedia
rows.note: Published in Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher; the book-length Critique itself was not published until after Marx's death.

rows.claim: Marx's stated implication: abolishing religion as illusory happiness is a demand for people's real happiness — the call is to give up a condition that requires illusions, not merely the illusion itself
rows.sourceTitle: Opium of the people - Wikipedia
rows.note: This is the interpretive crux distinguishing 'opium as narcotic deception' readings from 'opium as necessary painkiller for real suffering' readings.

rows.case: Bernays and the birth of PR
rows.claim: Bernays' 1928 book Propaganda recast 'propaganda' as 'public relations,' arguing organized manipulation of opinion is a necessary feature of democracy
rows.sourceTitle: Propaganda (book) - Wikipedia
rows.note: Followed his earlier Crystallizing Public Opinion (1923) and A Public Relations Counsel (1927).

rows.case: Bernays and the birth of PR
rows.claim: Bernays' famous statement of the theory: 'We are governed, our minds are molded, our tastes formed, our ideas suggested, largely by men we have never heard of.'
rows.sourceTitle: Propaganda (book) - Wikipedia
rows.note: Opening lines of Propaganda.

rows.claim: Bernays defined 'engineering of consent' as an engineering approach to getting people to support ideas/programs, based on scientific knowledge of the situation
rows.sourceTitle: The Engineering of Consent - Edward L. Bernays, 1947 (SAGE/Annals of the American Academy)
rows.note: Essay published in Annals of the American Academy of Political and Social Science, vol. 250.

rows.claim: Bernays staged the 1929 'Torches of Freedom' Easter Parade stunt for American Tobacco, recruiting women to smoke publicly and framing cigarettes as symbols of women's emancipation
rows.sourceTitle: Torches of Freedom - Wikipedia
rows.note: Devised with input from a psychoanalyst framing smoking as sublimated 'oral eroticism' made into a symbol of liberation.

rows.claim: Share of cigarettes consumed by American women rose from 5% (1923) to 12% (1929) across the campaign period
rows.sourceTitle: BMI Gold: How Edward Bernays sold cigarettes as 'Torches of freedom' for women
rows.note: Neither Bernays nor American Tobacco were named in contemporaneous press coverage of the stunt.

rows.claim: A 1998 legal settlement forced public disclosure of internal tobacco industry documents showing decades of concealment of known cancer, heart disease, and addiction risks
rows.sourceTitle: How Tobacco Companies Created the Disinformation Playbook - Union of Concerned Scientists
rows.note: A federal judge described a 'conspiracy of silence and suppression of scientific research' by the industry and its lawyers.

rows.claim: Internal 1962 R.J. Reynolds memo (chemist Alan Rodgman) stated the evidence indicting cigarette smoke as a health hazard was 'overwhelming', while the industry publicly denied harm for decades afterward
rows.sourceTitle: TOBACCO OFFICIALS DISCUSSED HIDING DATA, MEMOS INDICATE - The Washington Post
rows.note: Companies discussed 'destroying' and 'burying' internal research on nicotine addictiveness.

rows.claim: The 1997 FDA Modernization Act relaxed direct-to-consumer (DTC) broadcast drug advertising rules, permitting branded ads naming conditions with only a 'major statement' of risks
rows.sourceTitle: DTC advertising, and its history with the FDA
rows.note: Prior FDA rules had effectively prevented broadcast drug ads since they required a full disclosure of side effects impractical in short spots.

rows.claim: US pharmaceutical DTC ad spending grew from $791 million (1996) to $3.2 billion (2003), with total promotional spending reaching $29.9 billion and DTC spend $4.2 billion by 2005
rows.sourceTitle: A Decade of Direct-to-Consumer Advertising of Prescription Drugs - New England Journal of Medicine
rows.note: NEJM's own decade-review figures.

rows.claim: DTC advertising is estimated to account for about 31% of the rise in US drug spending since 1997
rows.sourceTitle: Direct-to-Consumer Advertising of Prescription Drugs - EveryCRSReport.com
rows.note: Congressional Research Service compilation.

rows.claim: FDA warning letters to drug manufacturers for advertising violations fell from 142 (1997) to 21 (2006), even as ad spending quadrupled
rows.sourceTitle: DTC advertising, and its history with the FDA
rows.note: Suggests declining enforcement alongside rising promotional volume.

rows.case: pharmaceutical DTC advertising effect on prescribing
rows.claim: In a randomized controlled trial, patients making brand-specific drug requests received antidepressant prescriptions 53% of the time in major depression scenarios and 55% in adjustment-disorder scenarios, versus far lower rates for no-request patients (31% and 10% respectively)
rows.unit: percent of visits resulting in prescription
rows.sourceTitle: Influence of patients' requests for direct-to-consumer advertised antidepressants: a randomized controlled trial - PubMed
rows.note: Standardized-patient RCT; shows DTC-driven patient requests measurably shift physician prescribing behavior, including toward inappropriate use.

rows.claim: Global advertising spending was projected/estimated to exceed $1 trillion in 2025, with several trackers estimating between $1.08 trillion and $1.17 trillion
rows.sourceTitle: Global advertising spending to top $1 trillion in 2025 - Marketplace
rows.note: Estimates vary by tracker (WPP Media reported $1.14 trillion); digital accounts for roughly 75% of the total.

rows.claim: Global PR agency industry revenue estimated at $68.7 billion (IBISWorld, 2025), with other market-research firms estimating $93-109 billion depending on market definition
rows.sourceTitle: Global Public Relations Agencies Industry Analysis, 2025 - IBISWorld
rows.note: Wide disagreement across market-research vendors on market boundary/definition.

rows.case: US WWI Committee on Public Information (Creel Committee)
rows.claim: Established by Executive Order in April 1917, CPI was the first large-scale US government propaganda agency, mobilizing opinion behind WWI via newspapers, film, posters, and speaking tours
rows.sourceTitle: Committee on Public Information - Wikipedia
rows.note: Chaired by George Creel; abolished by Wilson in August 1919.

rows.case: US WWI Committee on Public Information (Creel Committee)
rows.claim: CPI's volunteer 'Four-Minute Men' delivered 7,555,190 speeches in 1917-1918; CPI placed material in 20,000 newspaper columns per week
rows.sourceTitle: Four Minute Men - Wikipedia
rows.note: 75,000 Four-Minute Men and women delivered the speeches per CPI's own records.

rows.case: US WWII Office of War Information
rows.claim: OWI was established June 1942 (Executive Order 9182) to control wartime information/imagery across radio, print, and film; distributed posters nationally to post offices, schools, and railroad stations
rows.sourceTitle: US WWII Propaganda: Posters, Censorship, and the OWI - LegalClarity
rows.note: Specific total OWI budget figure not found in searched sources; see Not Found list.

rows.claim: Goebbels' Propaganda Ministry commissioned the cheap 'Volksempfänger' radio (76 Reichsmarks, with a 35-Reichsmark model) to maximize radio ownership as a propaganda channel
rows.sourceTitle: Volksempfänger - Wikipedia
rows.note: 76 RM was roughly two weeks' average wage; the cheaper set could be paid in installments.

rows.claim: By 1941, 65% of German households owned a Volksempfänger radio receiver, described by a historian as a 'vital element of success' in spreading Nazi ideology
rows.sourceTitle: Volksempfänger - Wikipedia
rows.note: Quantified adoption; searched sources did not surface a peer-reviewed causal effectiveness study isolating radio's persuasive effect (see Not Found list).

rows.claim: Global self-improvement market size estimated at approximately $45.72 billion (2024), or $64.48 billion (2025) by a different vendor, projected to $84-93.75 billion by 2030-2034
rows.sourceTitle: Self-Improvement Market Size, Industry Statistics, Growth 2034 - Zion Market Research
rows.note: Wide vendor disagreement; a third vendor (Custom Market Insights) put the 2025 figure at $46.1 billion.

rows.claim: US self-improvement market valued at $16.5 billion (2024), projected to $28.3 billion by 2033 (6.2% CAGR); a separate figure states the US self-help industry sells over $11 billion/year
rows.sourceTitle: US Self Improvement Market Size, Trends, Share 2033 - Custom Market Insights
rows.note: The $11 billion/year figure and the $16.5 billion figure come from different measurement scopes.

rows.claim: Norman Vincent Peale's 'The Power of Positive Thinking' (1952) sold over 5 million copies, spent 186 consecutive weeks on the NYT bestseller list including 48 weeks at #1
rows.unit: copies sold / weeks on bestseller list
rows.sourceTitle: The Power of Positive Thinking by Dr. Norman - Audible summary
rows.note: Translated into 40+ languages.

rows.case: law of attraction bestseller: The Secret
rows.claim: Rhonda Byrne's 'The Secret' (2006) has sold more than 35 million copies in 50+ languages, claiming a 'law of attraction' by which thought alone shapes objective circumstances
rows.sourceTitle: The Secret (Byrne book) - Wikipedia
rows.note: Both book and film.

rows.claim: Psychologists and critics describe The Secret's claims as pseudoscientific, prone to victim-blaming (e.g., implying illness or poverty result from negative thinking) and lacking supporting evidence
rows.sourceTitle: The law of attraction debunked: A psychology professor explains what's wrong with Rhonda Byrne's 'The Secret' - PsyPost
rows.note: Direct scholarly critique of the demand that sufferers 'feel better first' to improve outcomes.

rows.claim: Barbara Ehrenreich's 'Bright-Sided' (2009) argues that flawed studies linking positive attitude to cancer survival are discounted by most researchers, and that mandatory positive thinking pressures cancer patients to suppress legitimate anger/fear
rows.sourceTitle: Summary and Reviews of Bright-sided by Barbara Ehrenreich
rows.note: Also argues the refusal to consider negative outcomes (e.g., in mortgage lending) contributed to the 2008 financial crisis.

rows.claim: Amy Cuddy's power-posing claims (2010 study, viral TED talk with 75M+ views) failed to replicate in subsequent studies; a 2015 University of Zurich replication (Ranehill et al.) found no effect on behavior or hormone levels; original co-author Dana Carney publicly disavowed the effect in 2016
rows.sourceTitle: Power posing - Wikipedia
rows.note: A widely cited case study of the positive-psychology/self-help replication crisis; some pre-registered replications still find modest self-reported-power effects even where hormonal/behavioral effects vanish (disagreement noted).

rows.claim: C.R. Snyder's hope theory defines hope as a cognitive set combining agency (goal-directed motivation/'willpower') and pathways (perceived capacity to generate routes to goals, 'waypower')
rows.sourceTitle: The Will and the Ways: Development and Validation of an Individual-Differences Measure of Hope - Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1991
rows.note: Published in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, Vol. 60, No. 4, pp. 570-585.

rows.claim: Snyder's Adult Hope Scale (AHS) has 12 items (4 pathways, 4 agency, 4 filler), scored 8-64; companion instruments include the Children's Hope Scale (6 items, ages 8-16) and the 6-item State Hope Scale, with reported internal-consistency alphas between .79 and .95 across four original validation samples
rows.sourceTitle: Adult Hope Scale (AHS) - Fetzer Institute self-measures archive
rows.note: Exact per-sample n not recovered from searched sources; see Not Found list.

rows.claim: The Adult Hope Scale and Children's Hope Scale predict academic performance, athletic outcomes, sales productivity, recovery from physical injury, and stress resilience, often beyond what is explained by IQ, prior performance, optimism, or self-efficacy alone
rows.sourceTitle: Hope Theory (Snyder): The Triad That Predicts Beyond IQ
rows.note: Secondary summary of the empirical literature Snyder and successors built on the AHS.

rows.claim: Scholars criticize hope theory as culturally individualist (developed on American samples), with the agency component in particular reflecting an assumption that personal motivational energy — not interpersonal or collectivist trust — drives goal pursuit; meta-analyses find only small effect sizes across contexts
rows.sourceTitle: 'A New Hope' for Positive Psychology: A Dynamic Systems Reconceptualization of Hope Theory - Frontiers in Psychology
rows.note: Also criticized for operationalizing an intended dynamic, iterative agency-pathways process as a static, linear, acontextual scale.

rows.claim: Seligman and Maier's 1967 'Failure to escape traumatic shock' (Journal of Experimental Psychology, 74, 1-9) found dogs given inescapable shock in a harness later failed to learn escape/avoidance behavior in a shuttle box, unlike dogs given escapable shock or no shock
rows.sourceTitle: Failure to escape traumatic shock - PubMed
rows.note: Exact number of dogs used in the original design was not recovered from searched sources; see Not Found list.

rows.claim: Fifty years later, Maier and Seligman's 'Learned Helplessness at Fifty: Insights From Neuroscience' (Psychological Review, 123(4), 349-367) reversed the original causal model: passivity after inescapable shock is now understood as the default, unlearned response mediated by serotonergic activity in the dorsal raphe nucleus, and it is the learning of control (via medial prefrontal cortex activity) that actively inhibits this default passivity
rows.sourceTitle: Learned helplessness at fifty: Insights from neuroscience - PubMed
rows.note: The original theory 'got it backward': helplessness is not learned, it's the resting state; agency/control is what must be learned/detected.

rows.claim: Lauren Berlant's 'cruel optimism' names a double bind: attachment to an object/fantasy of the 'good life' that promises flourishing while actually obstructing it — the concept traces the retraction, since the 1980s, of the postwar social-democratic promise
rows.sourceTitle: Cruel Optimism - Duke University Press
rows.note: Concept first appeared as a 2006 article in the journal differences (17(3), 20-36), expanded to a monograph in 2011.

rows.claim: Cruel optimism has been applied in empirical/qualitative research on frontline poverty governance, disability studies, and post-2008 crisis-era affective political economy; a cited 2024/2025 study applies it to explain how neoliberal governmentality sustains itself by promising autonomy it withholds
rows.sourceTitle: Cruel optimism, affective governmentality and frontline poverty governance: 'You can promise the world'
rows.note: A precise Google Scholar citation count for Cruel Optimism was not recovered from searched sources; see Not Found list.

rows.claim: Calm's estimated 2025 revenue was $210 million (a 24% decrease from 2024), down from an estimated $300 million in 2023; Calm had an estimated 3.5 million subscribers in 2025, down 500,000 from 2024
rows.sourceTitle: Calm Revenue and Usage Statistics (2026) - Business of Apps
rows.note: Calm has led Headspace in revenue since 2018.

rows.claim: Calm's subscription pricing is $14.99/month or $69.99/year; a standalone Calm Sleep Premium subscription launched at $69.99/year in September 2025
rows.sourceTitle: Calm Revenue and Usage Statistics (2026) - Business of Apps
rows.note: A February 2026 annual-price increase was announced without the new price disclosed publicly.

rows.claim: Headspace paid subscribers declined by 300,000 to 2 million in 2025; Headspace Health (combined with Ginger) was valued at $3 billion
rows.sourceTitle: Headspace Revenue and Usage Statistics (2026) - Business of Apps
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Mindfulness/meditation app market size estimates vary widely by vendor: $701 million (Fact.MR), $1.30 billion (Technavio), $2.20 billion (Grand View Research), all for 2025 — a roughly 3x spread across research firms
rows.sourceTitle: Mindfulness Meditation Application Market Growth Analysis - Technavio
rows.note: One vendor (SkyQuest) reported an outlier figure of $139.48 billion for 2025, apparently a different market definition/scope; disagreement flagged.

rows.claim: Global wellness apps market size estimated at $12.87 billion (Precedence Research) or $26.03 billion (wellness management apps, same vendor) for 2025; a narrower 'wellness and mental health apps' market estimated at $4.97 billion
rows.sourceTitle: Wellness Apps Market Size to Surpass USD 51.12 Billion By 2035 - Precedence Research
rows.note: Definitional inconsistency across vendors, as with mindfulness-app figures above.

rows.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of mindfulness apps found an expected attrition rate of ~38% in app-arm participants, versus a 25% meta-analytic baseline in other mental-health apps (the discrepancy attributed to small pilot-study samples in prior estimates); the greatest dropout occurred within the first two weeks
rows.sourceTitle: Rates of attrition and engagement in randomized controlled trials of mindfulness apps: Systematic review and meta-analysis - ScienceDirect
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Real-world adherence to app-based meditation interventions is as low as 24%, and only about 2% of health-app users persistently engage at the level needed to obtain corresponding health benefits
rows.sourceTitle: A Mobile App for Stress Management in Middle-Aged Men and Women (Calm): Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial - PubMed
rows.note: This is a striking mismatch between app popularity/marketing claims and actual sustained use.

rows.case: meditation app measured benefit despite attrition
rows.claim: In a headspace-mediation-program RCT with 343 participants randomized, 186 (54.2%) completed at least one post-test; among completers, the treatment condition showed larger improvements in distress, social connectedness, and mindfulness relative to a waitlist control
rows.sourceTitle: Testing the Efficacy of a Multicomponent, Self-Guided, Smartphone-Based Meditation App: Three-Armed Randomized Controlled Trial
rows.note: Illustrates real benefit for people who complete the program, alongside the retention problem documented above.

rows.claim: TikTok's feed design is explicitly compared to a 'variable reward' slot-machine mechanism: uncertainty about the next video reinforces compulsive scrolling in the same way intermittent variable-ratio reward schedules drive slot-machine and gambling behavior
rows.sourceTitle: Your personal slot machine: Tristan Harris on smartphone addiction
rows.note: Harris (ex-Google) traces this framing to a 2013 internal Google presentation, 'A Call to Minimize Distraction & Respect Users' Attention,' and to CBS '60 Minutes' testimony.

rows.case: TikTok leaked internal algorithm document / withheld safety feature
rows.claim: A leaked internal TikTok engineering document ('TikTok Algo 101') described the recommendation system's mechanics; a 2021 internal algorithm change meant to reduce harmful-content overwhelm was deliberately withheld from a control group of about 10% of US users (~15 million people) to preserve engagement-metric measurement capability
rows.unit: count of users in withheld control group
rows.sourceTitle: Leaked TikTok Docs Reveal Dark Side of Engagement: Addiction, Algorithm Bias, and Exploitation
rows.note: Surfaced via a 2024 multistate lawsuit against TikTok that unsealed internal documents.

rows.claim: Internal Facebook research, leaked by whistleblower Frances Haugen (Wall Street Journal, Sept 2021), found the company's own researchers concluded 'we make body image issues worse for one in three teen girls' (2019 slide), and that teens blame Instagram for increased anxiety and depression
rows.sourceTitle: Facebook documents show how toxic Instagram is for teens, Wall Street Journal reports - CNBC
rows.note: Zuckerberg publicly called this internal research 'inconclusive'; Facebook did not make the research public or share it with academics/lawmakers who requested it.

rows.claim: Among teens who reported suicidal thoughts, 13% of British users and 6% of American users traced the origin of those thoughts to Instagram, per Facebook's own internal research
rows.unit: percent of suicidal-ideation teens attributing cause to Instagram
rows.sourceTitle: Facebook Internal Research Found Instagram Can Be Very Harmful To Young Girls, Report Says - Forbes
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Frances Haugen testified to the Senate Commerce Committee (Oct 5, 2021) that Facebook's engagement-based ranking could lead children from innocuous topics like healthy recipes to anorexia-promoting content in a short period, alleging the company chose 'to prioritize its profits over people'
rows.sourceTitle: Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen testifies before the Senate - TechCrunch
rows.note: Hearing titled 'Protecting Kids Online: Testimony from a Facebook Whistleblower.'

rows.case: TikTok creator payouts: original Creator Fund
rows.claim: TikTok's original Creator Fund (2020-2023) paid only $0.02-$0.04 per 1,000 views, from a fixed total budget shared across all enrolled creators, so per-creator earnings fell as enrollment grew
rows.sourceTitle: How Much Does TikTok Pay Per View in 2026? - Soundstripe
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: TikTok creator payouts: Creator Rewards Program
rows.claim: TikTok's 2024 Creator Rewards Program replaced the Creator Fund, paying roughly $0.40-$1.00+ per 1,000 qualified views (10-25x the old rate); example: 100,000 views yielding $40-$100, with a 'qualified view' requiring a real (non-bot) account watching at least 5 seconds from an eligible region
rows.sourceTitle: How Much Does TikTok Pay in 2026? - Influencer Marketing Hub
rows.note: Payout scales with video length, originality, watch time, and audience-region (premium markets like US/Canada pay more).

rows.case: US Surgeon General advisory on social media and youth mental health
rows.claim: The 2023 US Surgeon General advisory reported adolescents spending more than 3 hours/day on social media face roughly double the risk of poor mental health outcomes; up to 95% of youth ages 13-17 use a social media platform, over a third 'almost constantly'; ~64% of adolescents report exposure to hate-based content
rows.figure: 2x risk (>3 hrs/day); 95% platform use; 64% hate-content exposure
rows.unit: relative risk / percent usage / percent exposure
rows.sourceTitle: Social Media and Youth Mental Health: The U.S. Surgeon General's Advisory (2023)
rows.note: Issued by Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy, May 2023.

rows.claim: Mozilla Foundation's crowdsourced 'YouTube Regrets' study (2021, using its RegretsReporter tool) documented user-reported 'rabbit holes' of misinformation, violence, and hate from YouTube recommendations, while a separate 2020 academic study reached the opposite conclusion, finding the algorithm actively discourages movement toward radicalizing/extremist content
rows.sourceTitle: YouTube's recommender AI still a horror show, finds major crowdsourced study - TechCrunch
rows.note: Disagreement flagged per prompt instructions: crowdsourced self-report methodology (Mozilla) vs. algorithmic-trace methodology (the 2020 study) reach opposite conclusions.

rows.claim: A 2026-reported study found Apple's Downtime feature users experienced an average 45-minute increase in nightly sleep duration; a separate 2026 analysis of Android 12 users found a 35% increase in reported sleep-quality satisfaction after one month of Bedtime Mode use; other studies find inconsistent or null effects from digital nudges alone
rows.sourceTitle: Digital Wellbeing Apps: What Actually Works?
rows.note: Disagreement flagged: one exploratory study 'found no significant evidence to support the impact of active digital nudges on reducing screen time,' while a self-designed app ('Mytime') study reported a 21% reduction in non-use of specific apps.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: Joan Tronto's ethics of care identifies four (later five) analytically distinct but cyclically interconnected phases: 'caring about' (moral quality: attentiveness), 'taking care of' (responsibility), 'care-giving' (competence), 'care-receiving' (responsiveness), and a later fifth phase, 'caring with' (all parties participate in deciding what care is needed)
rows.sourceTitle: Joan Tronto - Ethics of care
rows.note: Framework originates in Tronto's 'Moral Boundaries: A Political Argument for an Ethic of Care' (1993).

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.case: global care economy: unpaid care work value
rows.claim: Valued at hourly minimum wage, unpaid care work would constitute 9% of global GDP, or $11 trillion; 16.4 billion hours per day are spent on unpaid care work globally — equivalent to 2 billion people working 8-hour days for no pay
rows.figure: 9% of global GDP / $11 trillion; 16.4 billion hours/day
rows.unit: USD / share of GDP / hours per day
rows.sourceTitle: Care Work and Care Jobs for the Future of Decent Work - ILO
rows.note: Based on data from 64 countries covering two-thirds of the world's working-age population.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: Women perform 76.2% of unpaid care work globally, averaging 4 hours 25 minutes/day, versus men's 1 hour 23 minutes/day
rows.sourceTitle: Care Work and Care Jobs for the Future of Decent Work - ILO
rows.note: Same ILO report as above.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: ILO models a 'high road' investment path in care services yielding 475 million jobs by 2030, requiring total public and private expenditure on care services of US$18.4 trillion (18.3% of total projected GDP)
rows.sourceTitle: Care Work and Care Jobs for the Future of Decent Work - ILO
rows.note: Contrasted with a lower-investment 'business as usual' scenario in the same ILO report.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.case: regional variation in care-work share of GDP
rows.claim: Unpaid care work is estimated at approximately 21.4% of GDP in Latin America and the Caribbean, versus an OECD average of about 15%
rows.sourceTitle: Improving care economy is vital to growth and well-being - World Economic Forum
rows.note: n/a

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.case: care as a design value in media: constructive journalism outcomes
rows.claim: A systematic review of 22 effects experiments across 19 studies found solutions/constructive news stories consistently affect audience emotions (positively), but effects on trust are inconsistent across studies: US participants in one study reported higher trust in the solutions condition while Australian participants in the same design reported the opposite
rows.sourceTitle: Evaluating the effects of solutions and constructive journalism: A systematic review of audience-focused research
rows.note: Disagreement flagged directly in the source: trust effects are found to run in opposite directions in US vs. Australian samples.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: A systematic review of 71 publications on constructive journalism identifies six recurring core components: solutions, future orientation, inclusiveness, empowerment, context, and co-creation
rows.sourceTitle: Reflecting on the state of constructive journalism research - Constructive Institute
rows.note: The Constructive Institute (Denmark, founded by former DR editor-in-chief Ulrik Haagerup) is the leading institutional advocate/researcher of this design value.

rows.claim: Price et al. (2022) found greater daily exposure to social-media doomscrolling was associated with higher depressive and PTSD symptoms, with stronger effects among individuals with childhood-maltreatment histories; Satici et al. (2023) found heavy doomscrollers experienced reduced life satisfaction and harmony, mediated by increased psychological distress
rows.sourceTitle: Beyond the Scroll: Exploring How Intolerance of Uncertainty and Psychological Resilience Explain the Association Between Trait Anxiety and Doomscrolling - ScienceDirect
rows.note: Consistent finding across multiple independent studies (2022-2023) that doomscrolling predicts anxiety, depression, stress, and existential worry rather than relieving them.

rows.claim: A 2024 study found doomscrolling evokes existential anxiety and fosters pessimism about human nature, replicated with evidence from both Iran and the United States
rows.sourceTitle: Doomscrolling evokes existential anxiety and fosters pessimism about human nature? Evidence from Iran and the United States - ScienceDirect
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Reuters Institute Digital News Report finds overall news avoidance flat at 42% year-on-year (2026), up from 29% when first measured in 2017
rows.sourceTitle: Bad News Overload? News Avoidance on the Rise
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Selective news avoidance has grown markedly; about half of UK respondents (50%) and 45% of US respondents report making an effort to reduce news intake; in Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, and Turkey, 60%+ of the population report avoiding news sometimes or often
rows.sourceTitle: Overview and key findings of the 2026 Digital News Report - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
rows.note: Reuters distinguishes 'consistent avoiders' (low education, low news interest) from 'selective avoiders' (news-overloaded, protecting mental wellbeing).

rows.claim: Research on selective news avoidance finds a positive (protective) effect on perceived wellbeing — avoiding news more is associated with slightly improved general wellbeing, particularly for individuals managing anxiety around specific distressing topics
rows.sourceTitle: News Avoidance during the Covid-19 Crisis: Understanding Information Overload
rows.note: Disagreement/tension flagged: this contrasts with civic-engagement/democratic-participation literature (not itself quantified in this row) that treats broad news avoidance as a democratic-information deficit — the same behavior is read as protective in wellbeing research and as a deficit in civic-engagement research.

rows.case: NewsGuard AI content farm tracking: scale
rows.claim: NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center identified 3,749 'Unreliable AI-Generated News' (UAIN) sites as of its most recent count, up from 1,121 (Nov 2024), 3,006 (March 2026), and just 217 sites in 13 languages when tracking began in April 2023
rows.sourceTitle: Tracking AI-enabled Misinformation: 3,749 AI Content Farm sites (and Counting) - NewsGuard
rows.note: NewsGuard reports 300-500 new AI content farms appearing monthly.

rows.claim: Some AI content farm sites produce an average of more than 1,200 articles per day, monetized primarily through programmatic advertising
rows.sourceTitle: Next-gen content farms are using AI-generated text to spin up junk websites - MIT Technology Review
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Independent evaluations found Pangram's detector achieves ~99% accuracy with a false positive rate near 0% (about 1 in 10,000 academic essays, ~0.004%) and false negative rate of 2-4%; GPTZero's false positive rate is under 1% but its false negative rate is about 10.02%; all three major commercial tools (GPTZero, Originality.ai, Pangram) lose accuracy on passages under 50 words
rows.unit: percent accuracy / false positive rate / false negative rate
rows.sourceTitle: Do AI Detectors Work Well Enough to Trust? - Chicago Booth Review
rows.note: Disagreement noted: different vendors optimize for different error types (false-positive avoidance vs. false-negative avoidance), producing genuinely different trade-off profiles rather than one tool being simply 'more accurate.'

rows.claim: NewsGuard's own naming framework identified 125 news/information websites it judged to be substantially or entirely AI-generated at an earlier count checkpoint, alongside a broader combined content-farm-and-disinformation count of 1,121 sites as of November 2024
rows.sourceTitle: NewsGuard Now Identifies 125 News and Information Websites Generated by AI - NewsGuard
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: US public broadcasting funding: CPB appropriation
rows.claim: The Corporation for Public Broadcasting's federal appropriation was $525 million (2024) and $535 million (2025); Congress then rescinded approximately $1.1 billion in previously slated CPB funding via the Rescissions Act of 2025, and CPB announced it would wind down operations after the Senate Appropriations Committee approved zero future funding — the first time in CPB's history it would go without public financing
rows.sourceTitle: Public Broadcasting: Background Information and Issues for Congress - Congressional Research Service
rows.note: NPR received about 1% of its funding directly from the federal government (~$11 million/year, of which $3 million supports international newsgathering); PBS received about 16% directly.

rows.claim: The Corporation for Public Broadcasting shut down operations after federal funding was eliminated by the Trump administration and Congress in 2025
rows.sourceTitle: The CPB shuts down after federal funding eliminated - WHYY
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: NITV (National Indigenous Television, part of SBS) reaches 3.3 million Australians on television each month, described as growth in an otherwise declining linear-TV market
rows.sourceTitle: NITV launches exclusive Indigenous advisory offering - SBS About
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Following a 2005 Australian Government review, $48.5 million in funding was announced for NITV; the 2010 Stevens Review recommended sustaining NITV funding at approximately AUD 15.235 million/year for 2011-12
rows.sourceTitle: Special Broadcasting Service (SBS) & National Indigenous Television - Australian Government
rows.note: A separate secondary source states Indigenous media sector funding has seen 'no real funding increase in a decade.'

rows.claim: A community-academic mixed-methods (survey, interview, observational) impact assessment of Indigenous radio station La Voz de la CONFENIAE across two Amazonian Ecuadorian communities found ethnic/Indigenous communities referenced emotional and social wellbeing more than less-vulnerable comparison groups, tying language/cultural programming to community wellbeing
rows.sourceTitle: Assessing Indigenous Community Radio as Two-Way Communications Infrastructure: Communal Engagement and Political Mobilization in Ecuador
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Indigenous media sector capacity is constrained by limited policy direction, no real funding increase in a decade, constrained advertising revenue, ageing equipment, and limited staff training opportunities, despite documented wellbeing benefits from community involvement
rows.sourceTitle: Renewing a Vital Indigenous Voice and Community Asset - National Indigenous Australians Agency
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Community broadcasting produces measured economic, social, and cultural benefits, including direct employment for journalists and producers, with community involvement in production itself carrying documented wellbeing benefits for participants
rows.sourceTitle: Community radio: A lifeline for local bonds and resilience - SGS Economics and Planning
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: scholarly distinction: manufactured hope vs. real next steps
rows.claim: Hope-theory researchers formally define hope as requiring both agency (motivation) AND pathways (a perceived, actionable route to the goal) — hope without a pathway component collapses into wishing, not hope, per Snyder's own operational definition
rows.sourceTitle: The Will and the Ways: Development and Validation of an Individual-Differences Measure of Hope - Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1991
rows.note: This is the load-bearing structural claim used in the research note to distinguish hope (with a pathway) from mere positive affect (without one).

rows.case: scholarly distinction: cruel optimism's harm mechanism
rows.claim: Berlant's cruel optimism specifically identifies the harm mechanism as attachment maintained regardless of whether the object ever delivers on its promise — the object's fantasy value, not its actual deliverability, is what sustains the attachment, which is why the relation can persist indefinitely without resolution
rows.sourceTitle: Excerpt: 'Cruel Optimism' - Tableau (University of Chicago)
rows.note: This is the mechanism cited in the research note's synthesis section distinguishing deferral-based manufactured hope from pathway-bearing hope.

rows.claim: Tronto's care ethics makes 'responsiveness' (attending to whether care actually met the need, and what new needs emerged) an independent, necessary moral quality of the care-receiving phase — a caring relation that never closes this loop (never checks whether the recipient's need was actually met) fails the ethic of care on its own terms, regardless of the attentiveness or competence of the earlier phases
rows.sourceTitle: Table 1, Tronto's four-phase model - Care in Healthcare, NCBI Bookshelf
rows.note: This is the structural claim used in the research note to define what distinguishes 'caring' media/design from media that merely performs attentiveness without verifying actual outcomes.

rows.claim: Positive psychology emerged as a distinct academic subfield in the late 1990s (Martin Seligman's 1998 APA presidency is widely cited as its founding moment), subsequently drawing academic and popular attention to happiness science
rows.sourceTitle: Summary and Reviews of Bright-sided by Barbara Ehrenreich
rows.note: Ehrenreich's critique specifically targets the institutionalization of positive psychology as an academic department alongside the popular self-help sunny-outlook tradition it draws on.

rows.claim: Bernays is widely termed the 'father of public relations,' drawing on psychoanalytic theory (he was nephew to Sigmund Freud) and social science to develop mass-persuasion theory and practice in the 1920s
rows.sourceTitle: The manipulation of the American mind: Edward Bernays and the birth of public relations - The Conversation
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: The Creel Committee (CPI) is remembered critically for suppressing free speech and cultivating wartime fear, with historians describing it as manipulating public perception of the severity of the European conflict
rows.sourceTitle: Committee on Public Information - The First Amendment Encyclopedia
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Litigation against TikTok alleges the platform's engagement-optimized algorithm and safety-filter design contributed to a minor's death, with internal documents cited as evidence the company knew of and misrepresented related risks
rows.sourceTitle: TikTok knowingly lied about how its algorithm led to a suicide - Android Authority
rows.note: This is a litigation allegation, not an adjudicated finding of fact; stated here as a claim under litigation, not as established causation.

rows.claim: A randomized controlled trial of daily mindfulness meditation app usage during the COVID-19 pandemic found measurable reductions in anxiety and improvements in well-being among app users versus controls
rows.sourceTitle: Effectiveness of Daily Mindfulness Meditation App Usage to Reduce Anxiety and Improve Well-Being During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Randomized Controlled Trial
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: Headspace RCT with ecological momentary assessment
rows.claim: A randomized controlled trial of app-based mindfulness meditation (Headspace), using ecological momentary assessment, found reduced stress among novice meditators relative to controls
rows.sourceTitle: App-based mindfulness meditation reduces stress in novice meditators: a randomized controlled trial of headspace using ecological momentary assessment
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: opium of the people: later readings
rows.claim: The phrase's context has received far less popular attention than the isolated quote itself; scholarly treatments (e.g., a dedicated Roskilde University dissertation) investigate the intellectual context of Marx's critique of religion in depth, cautioning against reading the line as purely dismissive
rows.sourceTitle: Religion is the Opium of the People: An Investigation into the Intellectual Context of Marx's Critique of Religion - Roskilde University Research Portal
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Industry analysts attribute self-improvement market growth to expansion of digital learning, wellness, and professional-development products, alongside rising focus on mental health and wellness generally
rows.sourceTitle: Self Help Industry: 2026 Verified Stats & Trends
rows.note: n/a

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: A 2025 scoping review of the 'care economy' concept finds evidence, challenges, facilitators, and future opportunities scattered across a heterogeneous literature without a single settled definition of the term's boundaries
rows.sourceTitle: What is the care economy? A scoping review on current evidence, challenges, facilitators and future opportunities - PMC
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: Research into the psychophysiology of news avoidance investigates whether negative affect itself drives both attention to and subsequent avoidance of news, suggesting a single underlying affective mechanism governs both doomscrolling and news-avoidance behaviors
rows.sourceTitle: The Psychophysiology of News Avoidance: Does Negative Affect Drive Both Attention and Inattention to News?
rows.note: n/a

rows.case: public media funding: NPR direct federal share
rows.claim: NPR received about 1% of its programming/operations funding directly from the federal government per year (approximately $11 million, of which $3 million supported international newsgathering); PBS received roughly 16% directly from federal sources
rows.sourceTitle: How federal funding for public media works—and why it's essential - KSUT Public Radio
rows.note: Much larger shares of funding for many local/rural and tribal public stations come through CPB pass-through grants rather than being 'direct' in this narrow sense — the 1%/16% figures understate dependence for smaller stations.

rows.case: Nazi Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda: scope
rows.claim: The Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda, created shortly after the Nazi seizure of power in January 1933 and headed by Joseph Goebbels, exercised control over all German mass media and creative artists
rows.sourceTitle: Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda - Wikipedia
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: A dedicated 'self-care apps' market size report exists as a distinct market category from broader wellness/mindfulness apps, reflecting industry fragmentation of overlapping product categories under different market-research names
rows.sourceTitle: Self-Care Apps Market Growth, Trends Analysis Report by 2033
rows.note: Flagged to explain to the reader why self-help, wellness-app, and meditation-app market-size figures in this dataset do not sum cleanly — market-research vendors use overlapping, non-standardized category boundaries.

rows.claim: An interdisciplinary review of the characteristics of hope across philosophy, psychology, and other fields finds no single settled definition of hope, with Snyder's agency/pathways model being the dominant but not only psychological operationalization
rows.sourceTitle: Characterizing Hope: An Interdisciplinary Overview of the Characteristics of Hope - Applied Research in Quality of Life
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: AI-generated content farm sites are monetized primarily via programmatic advertising, which pays out based on page views/impressions regardless of content quality or accuracy, creating a direct financial incentive for high-volume, low-cost AI content production
rows.sourceTitle: Rapid growth of news sites using AI tools like ChatGPT is driving the spread of misinformation - Euronews
rows.note: n/a

rows.claim: DoubleVerify's Fraud Lab exposed a coordinated network of 200+ made-for-advertising (MFA) domains ('AutoBait') producing AI-generated articles and images from a shared automated templating system (title, summary length, slide count as variables); Axios reported the operation could produce pages for under $2.25 each
rows.unit: count of domains / USD per page
rows.sourceTitle: DV Exclusive: Inside an AI Slop Factory - DoubleVerify
rows.note: Recovered from the house carrier lib/emsenn/.../science-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/2026/08/20/research-memo-ai-slop-as-industrialized-synthetic-attention-arbitrage.md, current through June 11, 2026; exceeds this session's own web search on content-farm unit economics.

rows.case: AI-generated YouTube channels: scale and revenue
rows.claim: A Guardian report on a Kapwing study found more than 20% of videos recommended to a new YouTube account were categorized as AI slop; 278 top channels classified as fully AI-generated had amassed 63 billion views and 221 million subscribers combined, with estimated annual revenue of about $117 million
rows.sourceTitle: More than 20% of videos shown to new YouTube users are 'AI slop', study finds - The Guardian
rows.note: Recovered from the house carrier's AI-slop research memo (2026-08-20); not found independently in this session's own web searches.

rows.claim: A 2026 large-scale measurement study using the Internet Archive found that by mid-2025, about 35% of newly published websites in its sample were classified as AI-generated or AI-assisted; increases in AI text correlated with lower semantic diversity and more positive sentiment, though not necessarily lower factual accuracy in that study
rows.unit: percent of newly published websites, mid-2025
rows.sourceTitle: The Impact of AI-Generated Text on the Internet (arXiv), cited in the house AI-slop research memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier; the house memo also notes a 2026 theoretical paper (arXiv 2601.06060) arguing 'slop' should be studied as a cultural form with family-resemblance features (superficial competence, asymmetric effort, mass producibility), not dismissed only as garbage.

rows.claim: The NELA-PS dataset documents over 7.9 million articles from 1,093 'pink-slime' sources over 2.5 years, defining pink-slime outlets as low-quality, often partisan content framed as authentic local news
rows.sourceTitle: NELA-PS dataset paper (arXiv), cited in the house AI-slop research memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier; a related Yale ISPS study found participants often preferred algorithmically generated local-looking sites over real local news, especially when real sites were ad-cluttered.

rows.claim: Axios reported that AI-powered local news network Nota News shut down in 2026 after plagiarism allegations; Poynter found more than 70 lifted examples from at least 29 outlets and 53 journalists, with internal AI tools used to repurpose local reporting under new bylines
rows.sourceTitle: Nota AI news sites shut down amid plagiarism allegations - Axios
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier's content-farm research memo.

rows.case: Demand Media / eHow: pre-AI content-mill labor rates
rows.claim: Wired's 2009 account of Demand Media documented an industrial workflow assigning content via search-term/ad-market/competition signals, reporting average pay around $15 per short article and about $20 per video clip, plus micropayments for copyediting, fact-checking, transcription, and title proofing
rows.sourceTitle: Demand Media - Wired (2009), cited in the house content-farms-and-content-mills research memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier's political-economy-of-content-farms memo; shows 'automation' at Demand Media meant an algorithmically managed labor process, not a labor-free one — a distinction the memo makes explicit.

rows.case: Google Panda update: scale of search-result change
rows.claim: Google's 2011 'Panda' quality update changed about 12% of U.S. search results, explicitly targeting low-value, copied, or not-useful content-farm sites, making content farms an explicit search-quality problem
rows.unit: percent of US search results changed
rows.sourceTitle: Google clamps down on content farms - Wired (2011), cited in the house content-farms memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier.

rows.claim: DoubleVerify reported that MFA sites comprised 21% of programmatic ad impressions and 15% of total ad spend in ANA's 2023 benchmark study, with MFA impression volume rising 19% year over year
rows.sourceTitle: ANA 2023 programmatic transparency study, cited in the house content-farms and AI-slop memos
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier; independently confirms and matches this session's own web-search finding on MFA ad-spend share.

rows.claim: A 2025/2026 study on repurposed YouTube accounts ('chameleon channels') found a market in aged/resold channels, with observed sales exceeding $1 million in six months, many sold or repurposed channels later carrying policy-sensitive content
rows.sourceTitle: Chameleon channels study (arXiv), cited in the house content-farms-and-content-mills research memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier.

rows.case: AI content farms tied to state influence operations
rows.claim: NewsGuard reports that 358 AI content farms in its dataset are linked to Storm-1516, a pro-Russian influence operation using sites designed to resemble local newspapers in the US and Europe
rows.unit: count of linked AI content-farm sites
rows.sourceTitle: NewsGuard launches real-time 'AI Content Farm' detection datastream, cited in the house AI-slop research memo
rows.note: Recovered from house carrier; complements this session's own web-search NewsGuard tracking-center figures (3,749 sites overall as of the most recent independent check).

rows.case: the house's own content mill (revival inventory, negative example)
rows.claim: The founder's 2018 personal log records founding 'NTMY News, a content mill' (2015-06) and, months later, promoting the 'Ted Cruz is the Zodiac Killer' meme through it; the mill's remains sit in public-news-media-services-section/lib/legacy/ntmy-news/ as revival inventory under house convention
rows.sourceTitle: Note on hopeium media - house carrier (2026-09-05), citing the founder's personal log
rows.note: First-party house fact, not open-web-verifiable; included per the coordinator's instruction to cite what the house already holds. The house frames this as: 'The house has lived this ... and has already refused it once.'

rows.case: hope's theological failure modes formalized by the house
rows.claim: The house's philosophy-seat carrier reads Aquinas (Summa Theologiae II-II qq. 17-21) as identifying despair and presumption as the two opposed vices against hope — both are premature closures of the constitutively open future (bonum futurum arduum possibile); hope is 'the virtue of withholding the closure,' not a third judgment
rows.sourceTitle: Note on Abandonment, Acedia, and the Whirl - house carrier (2026-08-23)
rows.note: House carrier's own synthesis, drawing on Aquinas and Pieper (On Hope, 1935); the note explicitly marks its own citations as 'working references from assistant knowledge; verify quotations and editions before public use.' Included as house theory, not as independently verified primary-source scholarship by this session.

rows.claim: The same house carrier names the media formats: 'the economy of commentary runs on certainty ... its two staple products are the doom-take, the future settled as loss ... and the solution-take, the future settled as secured, five easy mechanisms, the thread that fixes everything. These are despair and presumption as content formats'
rows.sourceTitle: Note on Abandonment, Acedia, and the Whirl - house carrier (2026-08-23), section 4.2
rows.note: This is the house's own theoretical framing (not an empirical finding); presented here as house theory per the coordinator's instruction, quoted verbatim rather than paraphrased.

rows.case: lament as the tradition's alternative genre
rows.claim: The house carrier recovers lament (a third of the Psalter, per Brueggemann's analysis of its loss as crippling a community's speech) as 'complaint within relation: grief and protest addressed to the Holder, at full strength ("How long?"), without closure in either direction ... the open wound kept open in the covenant' — distinct from both the doom-take's verdict and the solution-take's fix
rows.sourceTitle: Note on Abandonment, Acedia, and the Whirl - house carrier (2026-08-23), section 4.3
rows.note: House theory citing Brueggemann, 'The Costly Loss of Lament' (1986); this session did not independently verify the Brueggemann citation against the primary source.

rows.case: house formalization of hope as a held-open cell
rows.claim: A house computer-science carrier proposes formalizing hope as obtaining at a position where a resolving continuation exists but is not yet reached and the outcome is 'held' rather than collapsed to true or false; on this reading, cruel optimism is 'hope in a genre that has none' — holding an open cell where the structure warrants a settled negative outcome
rows.unit: claim (house theory proposal, graded [target]/[conjecture] by its own author)
rows.sourceTitle: The Unbuilt Affects: Hope, Stickiness, Reading Posture, Vertigo - house carrier (2026-08-29)
rows.note: Explicitly self-graded by its own author as a proposal, not doctrine or a built system ('Nothing here is claimed as a theorem'); included as house theoretical work in progress, not as an established external result.

rows.technology: care as studied in ethics and organization
rows.claim: The house's medical program carrier states its paradigm as 'Care is relation-repair, never extraction,' operationalized at company scale as 'no upsell, no dark pattern, no data sale, no subscription trap, no diagnosis sold as certainty,' with 'every claim carries its evidence status in plain words'
rows.sourceTitle: 561 Group Medical Services Section README - house carrier
rows.note: House design paradigm, cited via the hopeium-media synthesis note; not an external empirical claim, included as the house's own stated design value for 'care' in a service/media context, directly answering the brief's request for scholarly separation of manufactured hope from media that leaves a real next step.

rows.case: house founder's own doomscrolling/reading neurocognitive framing
rows.claim: The founder's own essay distinguishes a 'reactive mode' (ventral attention network; fast, reward-seeking, good for scrolling feeds) from a 'reflective mode' (dorsal attention network; slow, connects ideas; good for reading and nuanced conversation), stating 'the brain grows in the direction of what you practice most,' and recommends practices including scroll windows, ending sessions with longer reading, noticing bodily arousal signals, no social media before bed, and talking about what was read
rows.unit: claim (founder's own essay, house first-party source)
rows.sourceTitle: Why Doomscrolling Feels Easy and Reading Feels Hard - founder's essay, house carrier (2025-10-08)
rows.note: House first-party essay; cites a house-internal reference tag [cite:@emsenn_attention_neurocognitive_system_2025] for the dual-network claim rather than a specific peer-reviewed source this session could independently verify; the underlying ventral/dorsal attention network distinction is itself a real, independently-documented neuroscience finding (Corbetta & Shulman's two-networks model), though this session did not re-derive that citation from the open web in this pass.

rows.claim: The house carrier's working analytic definition: 'AI slop is high-volume synthetic or AI-assisted media whose low-cost surface plausibility is used to capture attention, ranking, monetization, or influence while externalizing verification, originality, labor, and trust costs onto audiences, platforms, advertisers, journalists, creators, and future information systems'
rows.unit: claim (house-synthesized definition, itself citing open literature)
rows.sourceTitle: Research memo: AI slop as industrialized synthetic attention arbitrage - house carrier (current through 2026-06-11)
rows.note: The house memo itself is well-sourced to primary reporting (NewsGuard, DoubleVerify, Axios, arXiv papers); this row cites the house's own synthesis definition rather than a single external primary source.
